name: Italian Republic

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 295,720 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Low/high allow for the Natural Earth polygon vs official figure and inland water (surface area is a few % larger).

population.note: asOf 2025: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 58,915,656. Range allows for 2026 drift and census revisions.

activePersonnel.note: IISS as quoted: 160,400 active (excludes 179,250 Carabinieri/Guardia di Finanza paramilitary). CIA Factbook 2025: ~170,000 (high). World Bank 338,000 (2020) includes Carabinieri.

trainedReserves.note: IISS as quoted: 14,500 reserves. Italy has no conscript reserve since 2005.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 160,400 minus infantry P roles (18,000). Covers navy and air force personnel, armour/artillery/air-defence crews, logistics, staff, training and other support.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to WWII Italy (~4.5-5 million mobilized from ~44 million, ~11%) scaled down for an all-volunteer force and an old population.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized infantry (Bersaglieri, Freccia/Dardo battalions) x ~500. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Italian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly below): Freccia 8x8 modern, Dardo dated.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army): Professional; Lebanon/Iraq/Baltics deployments.

count.note: Educated guess. Alpini (2 brigades), Folgore paratroopers, San Marco marines and light infantry. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Italian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly below): Lince mobility, Spike ATGM.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly above): Alpini and Folgore are well-trained long-service units.

count.note: Equipment list: Ariete C1 110 + Ariete C2 3 (87 on order). High: 200 Ariete delivered in total. Leopard 2A8 and KF51 programmes not delivered.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical): Ariete is a weak 1990s tank, upgrade underway.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

count.note: Equipment list: Dardo 198 + Freccia ~450 (630 planned, 249 first phase) + Centauro 259 + Centauro 2 ~100 delivered (150 listed) + Puma 6x6 200 + Bv206S armoured 112 = ~1,319. Centauro wheeled tank destroyers counted here. ~1,900 Lince IMVs excluded.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Mixed: Freccia/Centauro 2 modern, Puma and M113 old.
Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly below): PzH 2000 good; FH70 old.

count.note: Inventory: Eurofighter F-2000A 79 + F-35A 42 + F-35B 5 (Air Force) + F-35B 10 (Navy) = 136.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly above): F-35A/B plus Typhoon.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly above): Professional, Baltic/Icelandic air policing.

count.note: Inventory: Tornado IDS 19 + AV-8B+ Harrier II 11 (navy) = 30. AMX retired.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly below): Tornado and Harrier are old airframes being replaced by F-35.

count.note: Army equipment list: A129 37, CH-47C/F 21, NH90 59, AB-206 29, AB-205 37, AW169 1 = 184; Air Force (aircraft list): AW101 12, AW139 30, AW169 5 = 47; Navy: SH-101 10, SH-90 45, MH-90 10, SH-212 22 = 87. Total 318, trainers excluded.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly below): NH90/AW101 modern; A129 and Agusta-Bell utility old.

count.note: MQ-9A 4 (2 on order) + Army RQ-7B Shadow 16 = 20.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Small MQ-9 fleet.

count.note: Active ships list: aircraft carriers/LHD 2 (Cavour, Trieste) + destroyers 2 (Horizon) + frigates 15 (FREMM, PPA counted as frigates by the list) = 19.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly above): Cavour with F-35B, FREMM/Horizon with Aster.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly above): Professional, Red Sea operations 2024.

count.note: Amphibious ships 3 (San Giorgio LPDs) + OPV 9 + patrol 6 + minehunters 10 = 28.
Attack submarines: 4 Todaro (Type 212A) + 4 Sauro; the list header gives 9.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly below): Type 212A modern, Sauro old.

count.note: Army: SAMP/T 5 fire units (+1 NG), GRIFO 2 (Skyguard Aspide retired 2025), Skynex 1, Stinger 145 launchers (~12 batteries); Air Force SAMP/T/SPADA-MAADS not itemised. Total ~22.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly below): SAMP/T NG arriving.

commandQuality.note: Rubric commandQuality 0.75 (trained staff system, proven commanders) (slightly below): NATO-integrated staff, Rapid Deployable Corps HQ (Solbiate Olona); long peacekeeping experience, no high-intensity combat.

cohesion.note: Rubric cohesion 0.75 (professional with strong unit identity) (slightly below): Professional force; Alpini and Folgore strong unit identity.

morale.note: Rubric morale 0.5 (average): Average; low public appetite for war abroad.

weapons.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Storm Shadow, Aster, Spike, Meteor.

armor.note: Anchor 9: Ariete is a 1990s design without APS.

ships.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Carriers with F-35B, FREMM, 212A.

fortification.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Hardened air bases; limited GBAD.

logistics.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: KC-767/C-130J/C-27J airlift; Mediterranean basing.

communications.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Sicral 2 satcom, Link 16.

isr.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: COSMO-SkyMed radar satellites, MQ-9.

air.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: F-35A/B 5th generation in service.

cyber.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Joint cyber command (COR).

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 2,528,168,964,530 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD x 0.8005) / population 58,915,656 = 42,912. Range +/-10%.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 3,158,237,307,345 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 2,528,168,964,530 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS: 1.89% of GDP in 2025 (mid), 1.59% in 2024, 1.61% in 2021. Low is the lowest of those years; high allows ~5% for NATO-definition spending above SIPRI.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 22.6% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-1.5 pp for year-to-year variation.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Net importer of grain and feed, exporter of wine, olive oil, processed food.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 28,814,684 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 5.170% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 297,928. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

helicopters.note: Educated guess. Leonardo Helicopters (AW149, AW169, AW249, NH90 assembly).

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Cameri F-35 FACO and Eurofighter Caselle work share.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Iveco-OTO Melara (Freccia, Centauro 2); Leonardo-Rheinmetall JV from 2026.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Fincantieri builds FREMM-EVO, PPA, DDX.

roadKm.note: As quoted: 487,700 km, all paved (2007); 6,700 km autostrada.

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 17,305 route-km (IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). Low allows for closures since.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 123 ports, 12 large + 11 medium = 23; low counts large ports only.

merchantTonnage.note: UNCTAD 2025 as quoted: 7,226 thousand DWT under the Italian flag. High is an educated guess for Italian-owned foreign-flag tonnage (MSC is Swiss-based and excluded).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. By analogy to NATO mechanized brigade sustainment (truck-based, depots every ~150-200 km).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys, not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists only nine nuclear-armed states. Italy hosts US B61 bombs (Aviano, Ghedi) under NATO nuclear sharing (FAS lists Italy among host countries); not counted.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: Alpine and Apennine mountain terrain, fortified cities, population support; long peninsula gives some depth.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:ITA (World Bank); San Marino and Vatican City excluded (Vatican has its own snapshot). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from Wikipedia inventory tables (Italian Army equipment list, active Italian military aircraft list, active navy ship list) and IISS as quoted; ships_major = carriers/LHD + destroyers + frigates; Centauro wheeled tank destroyers counted in ifv_apc. drones = Group 2+ only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Carabinieri excluded although they include a military police brigade.
